paragraphs.source_en: “Yes. Then Mr. Yagi said, ‘Today is a gathering of ladies, and I have deliberately told the story above because I have something in mind. It may be rude of me to say so, but women, as a rule, have a fault: when they want to do something, they often do not take the direct shortcut from the front, but go about it by a roundabout route from far away. Of course, this fault is not limited to women; even men of the Meiji era, under the ill effects of civilization, have become somewhat feminine. Thus many of them waste a great deal of needless trouble and labor, and mistakenly suppose that this is the proper course, the policy a gentleman ought to adopt. Such people are malformed children bound by the evil consequences of enlightenment and civilization, and there is no need to discuss them further. But as for you ladies, I hope you will remember as well as possible the old tale I have just told, and when the decisive moment comes, handle matters with the honest mind of Foolish Take. If all of you become Foolish Takes, then the hateful frictions that arise between husband and wife, and between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, will surely be reduced by one third. The more schemes a person has, the more those schemes rebound upon him and become a source of misfortune. Therefore, the reason many women are, on average, far more unhappy than men is precisely that they are too fond of scheming and are not candid enough in affairs. Please, all of you, become Foolish Takes. That was Mr. Yagi’s speech.”
